contract_authorship: The two full-forall contracts were manually authored from the intended mathematics and source signature, before compiling the audit; they were not generated from Lean printed types.

semantic_review.object: Finite scalar expression syntax with genuine input, real constants, signed scaling, addition, products, finite sums, supported closed-form activations, coupled softmax, and epsilon LayerNorm.
semantic_review.algorithm: splitEval is a concrete structural recursion using constPair, addPair, scalePair, polarized mulPair, verified scalar activation pairs, verified multivariate softmax heads, and the explicit population-variance LayerNorm pair.
semantic_review.exactness: For every input index universe, every expression, and every arbitrary real input-stream pair, subtraction of splitEval equals ordinary eval on input differences. No positivity assumption is imposed on this algebraic identity.
semantic_review.convex_monotone_nonnegative: For every convex domain and every family of convex, monotone, nonnegative input stream functions, splitEval produces two convex, monotone, nonnegative stream functions on that domain.
semantic_review.layernorm: The constructor requires epsilon>0. Its ordinary operation uses the genuine population mean, variance, inverse square root and signed affine gain/bias; the split relies on the proved nonnegativity of represented variance.
semantic_review.softmax: An output index in Fin d witnesses d>0, excluding the undefined all-masked softmax case. An empty finite sum is nevertheless supported.
semantic_review.nonvacuity: A nonlinear expression combines a true two-coordinate softmax, negative scaling, two-coordinate LayerNorm and Gaussian GELU. It is checked on both constant inputs and nonconstant independent stream coordinates over a nonempty orthant.
semantic_review.boundaries: Negative stream inputs remain covered by exactness; a checked counterexample prevents interpreting the result as global monotonicity outside the nonnegative domain.
scope_limits: The expression theorem does not itself identify a complete Transformer architecture; a separately verified Transformer compiler is required.
Expression semantics do not certify shared-DAG size bounds, floating-point stability, or runtime.
The regularity theorem is compositional; raw signed-input monotonicity is not a conclusion.

boundary_consumer.development_note: A direct deeply nested regularity specialization initially exhausted elaboration heartbeats. The final consumer first proves a generic expression result and supplies the input domain type explicitly, avoiding accidental inference of E=Nat. No production theorem or hypothesis was changed.
